chapter: Long Branch and the war years
title: John Malachi's band at Dykes Stockade and Crystal Caverns, 1943
summary: Malachi took six players to Dykes, which closed with gas rationing; Benny Carwell then hired the band at Crystal Caverns on Willie Bryant's recommendation, with Charlie Rouse, Osie Johnson and Tommy Potter, from February 1943.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: So then he got this gig in...

Yeah. He got one out in Dykes Stockade. When that one was over, John got this job at the Dykes, and then he took six pieces out there. He took me, he took Cragbrains and Curtis, and Tommy Potter on bass...
This was when he took them from 26th Street to the other gig. Is that what you're saying?
But that gig folded up. John just got the gig together himself.
But this is the next gig.

Yeah. And then we stayed out there until Dykes closed down on account of... At that time, gas was rationed. People couldn't get no gas. So he claimed that he couldn't make no money, and he couldn't afford a band. So he just like that cut us off.
In the meantime, Benny Carwell wanted a band up at Crystal Caverns. He owned the place. So Willie Bryant, who was a helluva MC...
Is he the one from New York?

Yeah. So Willie Bryant told him, said, 'Man, why don't you get that band out there at Dykes? They're cookin', man. They're a good band. They can play these shows.' So Carwell hired us... You know, he's full of shit anyway; we had to give him hell, you know. There was a lot of things he was talking about he wanted us to do. He didn't want to pay no money, not what you were supposed to be getting. So we put in a notice a couple of times, and we were prepared to leave, and he came up with the money. The War was on then, and he had people standing out in the line to get in that place every night.
So it's the personnel in that photograph. John Malachi, Charlie Rouse on tenor, Osie Johnson on drums, Tommy Potter on bass...
Yeah. Harry Curtis on alto. I'm on trumpet.
You're on trumpet and John's on piano.
That started in what part of '43?
